contents.text:
I'm skipping the ADRs since the runtime view already covers this. The answer is in src/docs/architecture/06-runtime-view.md, which describes the tool loop as running up to 10 rounds with every call passing the guards first. I'm weighing whether to include the StreamPromptAsync snippet from that page, though it isn't required.

I'm leaning toward a prose answer with a short list of steps, without any code. The doc path goes on its own line at the end, just before the closing offer. I'll skip inventing an address for the tool loop since the page only shows it as a layer in the diagram.

The model asks for a tool, and the engine's `FunctionInvokingChatClient` runs it. Every call goes through `ToolCallGuards.InvokeAsync` first. The result goes back to the model, and the loop repeats until the model answers.

The steps, in order:

1. The engine sends the model the conversation, the system prompt and the tool list.
2. The model replies with one or more tool calls, which can come in the same round.
3. Each call is logged and then run. Its arguments arrive as data, never as shell text.
4. A result over 50,000 characters is summarised by a separate model call with no tools. If that fails, it is cut short.
5. A call cut off by the 16,000-token output limit is never run. The model is asked to continue in chunks.
6. If a tool throws, the exception message goes back to the model, so it can correct itself.
7. The result is added to the conversation, and the model continues. This repeats for up to 10 rounds per message.

On the last round the tools stay on the request, with tool use switched off. The model then has to answer in text. A sub-session also has a prompt budget. Past it, the subagent keeps its tools but cannot call them, and it answers from what it has.
